note-a.text: A keeps today's icon-row layout but swaps the icons for cells: each cell is the modifier itself, the current one solid-filled, and the final number moves to the left in the same slot Fireteam Purity already uses. Closest to a drop-in replacement for RangeInput.jsx.

note-b.text: B keeps the physical ruler metaphor the app already has (RulerIcon) and adds a pin so the selected band still reads as a point on a tape measure, not a menu of buttons.

note-c.text: C borrows the rulebook chart's idea that bar height should tell you the size of the modifier, but restrained to one hue per side instead of red/yellow/green/blue — answers 'do we want all that color' with 'the shape, not the palette'.

note-d.text: D is the most compact: a stepper plus a 7-dot sparkline. Best if the Range row ever needs to shrink, but the modifier-per-band view is smallest here too — a hover/tap shows it, nothing is visible at rest beyond the current value.

note-e.text: E takes the reciprocity requirement literally: since it's one distance, it's one ruler, with both weapons' modifiers stacked in each cell instead of two separate synced rows. Bigger change — Active and Reactive currently live in separate Grid columns — but it makes the shared value the point instead of an implementation detail. Every board above already demonstrates the sync live: click a band on either row and both rows (in A-D) move together, because both are driven by one shared bandIndex, exactly like rangeCm is shared in useMatchup.js today.

note-f.text: F answers 'can we keep yellow/blue/green/red': yes, but mapped by MOD VALUE (−3 always yellow, 0 always blue, +3 always green, −6 always red — that's the rulebook's own code, not something invented here), desaturated into a translucent tint so it sits on dark instead of shouting. Selection is a separate layer: an accent pin plus a halo in the row's teal/pink, so picking a band never overwrites the tier color underneath it. Best of both worlds if the rulebook color code is something players already read at a glance and shouldn't lose.
